open_points.subject: Import confirmation after an identical file is uploaded again
open_points.text: A16 rule 2 says another upload replaces the uploaded file, “one of the same bytes included,” and required test 3 says the earlier confirmation is refused “also when the new file has the same bytes.” But A13 rule 6 binds an import confirmation only to the action, target, absence of a revision/access version, and the inputs—“for the import, the file's digest and the picks”—while M11 gives the pending confirmation no upload identity or generation. Uploading a byte-identical file also is not stated to clear the pending confirmation.
open_points.question: How can Registry distinguish the replaced upload from the new byte-identical upload, and must an accepted upload invalidate an already pending import confirmation?
options: Treat every accepted upload as a distinct generation and bind the confirmation to that generation.
Clear any pending import confirmation whenever another file is successfully uploaded.
Treat byte-identical uploads as the same bound file, allowing the earlier confirmation, contrary to A16.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the old confirmation by treating each accepted upload as a distinct generation and binding import confirmation to that generation.

witness.initial: One valid owner session holds uploaded file F; its mapping has no errors, and Registry has shown confirmation C bound to digest d(F), the picks and mapping inputs.
events: The owner uploads F again in the same session with exactly the same bytes.
Within ten minutes, the owner submits C with the same picks and mapping inputs.
outcomes: Under A13's stated binding and lifecycle, C is still pending, its file digest and all inputs match, so the import may be accepted.
Under A16 rule 2 and required test 3, the second upload replaced the file C named even though its bytes are identical, so the submission is refused.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a committed import or a refusal requiring a new confirmation step.
